clue.text: Expert change to steam railway

indicators.note: change tells us to rework the letters into a new order here

explanation.surface: Someone praises a skilful conversion of a steam railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges STEAM plus RLY into MASTERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterly work is that of an expert, so the two are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Reckless ADC cuts the diagram

indicators.note: cuts means one piece slices into the middle of another piece

parts.note: a map is a diagram of an area

explanation.surface: An aide-de-camp recklessly slices through a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: ADC (aide-de-camp) looks like a person doing the cutting, but here it is simply the letters going in.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme is wild and impulsive, a synonym for reckless.

clue.text: Frightened editor has a wound that's healed

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a healed wound

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is nervous despite an old injury having healed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared and frightened are straightforward adjective synonyms for being afraid.

clue.text: Rabbits seen up Scots hill with trees

indicators.note: in a down clue, seen up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: brae is the Scottish word for a hillside
ash trees, in the plural

explanation.surface: Rabbits are spotted high on a wooded Scottish hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbits' looks like animals, but it is the verb meaning chatters on; 'seen up' turns BRAE into EARB.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (rabbit on) is British slang for talking at length, as one who earbashes does.

clue.text: Delivery of honey is a task undertaken for pleasure

parts.note: labour is the process of delivering a baby
taken as written
honey and love are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Gathering honey is a job done out of sheer enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a parcel, but it is childbirth; 'honey' is a pet name, not the food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes work done willingly for its own sake rather than for payment.

clue.text: Plains discovered by fool with map going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means the letters run from right to left

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A fool with a map heads west and finds the open plains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns the whole of SAPMAP round.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of South America.

clue.text: Was bothered about a deli

indicators.note: about suggests the letters move around into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone was troubled about what went on at a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges A DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ailed is to have been troubled or unwell, so the past-tense verbs match.

clue.text: Description of wine: half of it must be swallowed by a topsy-turvy sailor

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside another piece
topsy-turvy means upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned round

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word leaves just its first letter

explanation.surface: Tasting notes for a wine that a drunken sailor gulps half of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topsy-turvy' turns TAR into RAT; 'half of' it gives I, which 'must be swallowed by' puts inside to make RAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait can be a vivid verbal description, not just a painting.

clue.text: A magical feeling of celebrity: Hoffman's not in

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: not here means the following word is left out of the name

parts.note: Dustin Hoffman is the American film actor

explanation.surface: Fame's magic is missing because the actor Hoffman has not turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from DUSTIN, leaving DUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a dreamy, magical quality or feeling of romance or glamour.

clue.text: Criticism of help returned to the people

indicators.note: returned means the word is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a people or community

explanation.surface: Disapproval of aid sent back to a community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a form of harsh criticism.

clue.text: Girl who makes you nearly glow, then look back

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops just short of its final letter
look back means the synonym is read in reverse

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: A girl so lovely she nearly makes you glow and turn for a second look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops W from GLOW; 'back' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Gloria is one particular female first name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Treated with distemper to go red and clean

parts.note: to colour is to blush, going red
washed means cleaned

explanation.surface: A sick dog is dosed, turns red and is bathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distemper' suggests the dog disease, but it is a kind of water-based paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a cheap wall paint, and colourwashed walls are coated with such a tinted wash.

clue.text: Place for activities, but Karen can't start one

indicators.note: can't start means the name loses its first letter

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Karen cannot begin a game at the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't start' drops K from KAREN, leaving AREN.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue where sports and other events take place.

clue.text: Mixed-up, so not applied for

definitions.meaning: never requested, as goods not ordered from a supplier

explanation.surface: Muddled, so never requested.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both without order and not having been ordered from a supplier.

clue.text: Time after time they should get the order right

definitions.text: Time after time they should get the order right

parts.words: Time after time they should get the order right
parts.note: records listing dates one after another, whose whole job is to put events in the correct sequence

explanation.surface: Things that ought to get the sequence right every single time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' reads as 'repeatedly', but literally describes lists of successive dates.
explanation.definitionFit: These are arrangements of events in the order of their occurrence in time.

clue.text: Love's forbidding, without being unperfumed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
dour means stern and forbidding
less means without, as in 'less tax'

explanation.surface: Love is forbidding when it comes without any scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is a tennis score, nil, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without any smell is unperfumed.

clue.text: Area of companionship (short clue to "unexciting")

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: bland means dull, unexciting

explanation.surface: A friendly district given an abbreviated and dull clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops E from CLUE, leaving CLU.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubland is the London district of gentlemen's clubs around St James's, a social scene.

clue.text: Knock down farm animal, nearly twelve

parts.note: a bull is a farm animal

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a dozen is twelve

explanation.surface: A bull rampages, almost a dozen times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops N from DOZEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a building is to demolish it, knocking it down.

clue.text: French aviator's "Oui" drowned by bells shaken with violence

indicators.note: drowned by means submerged inside another piece
shaken means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a riot is an outbreak of violence

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's 'yes' is drowned out by violently pealing bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges the bells into LSBLE, and the French 'yes' sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Bleriot was the French pioneer who first flew an aeroplane across the English Channel in 1909.

clue.text: I shall have nothing to eat, which prevents infection

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone vows to eat nothing as protection against germs.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine is used as an antiseptic to keep wounds from becoming infected.

clue.text: Tickets for parking donkeys

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: Permits for leaving your donkeys in a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes are tickets or permits granting entry or travel.

clue.text: Lager spilled in B-road in smart part of London

indicators.note: in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: B, then road as via (Latin for road)

indicators.note: spilled means the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Beer is spilt on a minor road in an upmarket London district.
explanation.walkthrough: A B-road is a minor British road; the spilled lager (ELGRA) sits between the B and the VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgravia is an expensive, fashionable residential district of central London.

clue.text: Stumbles into river to catch fish

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps
eels are fish

explanation.surface: An angler stumbles into a river trying to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or stumble unsteadily.

clue.text: This girl's half way through race carrying a hod

indicators.note: carrying means one piece holds another inside it
half way through takes just the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A girl is halfway through a race while carrying a builder's hod.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is a bricklayer's open trough for carrying bricks on the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Rhoda is one particular female first name, so it stands for this girl.

clue.text: Loved and respected with trouble left behind

indicators.note: behind means the word just before is placed after the earlier piece

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
red describes the political left

explanation.surface: Cherished and honoured, with all difficulties put in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' reads as abandoned, but 'left' is the political colour and 'behind' places it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means deeply loved and admired, covering both senses.

clue.text: There's no end of cheese around Rio, so bye-bye

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps another
no end of means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Cheese is laid out around Rio, so it is time to say farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheerio is British slang for goodbye; 'no end of' strips the last E, and the remainder wraps round the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, in the plural as a casual farewell.

clue.text: Formal doctor's written essay does not get an "A"

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: does not get an means the letter named is missing from the word

explanation.surface: A doctor's formal essay fails to earn a top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does not get an' removes the A from ESSAY, leaving ESSY; the surface suggests an A grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and formal.

clue.text: Greek hero, anybody's other half's curious uses

indicators.note: the other half means the second half of the word
curious means odd, so the letters take an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: A Greek hero puts anyone's partner to strange purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other half' takes ODYS from ANYBODYS; 'curious' rearranges USES as SEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the hero of Homer's Odyssey, king of Ithaca.
